proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement contains no indemnity provisions at all, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 assume they exist (Section 9.3 expressly cross-references "the remedies required by Section 20.5"). We have inserted our standard Section 20: Vendor defends and indemnifies us for third-party IP infringement, breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and our own indemnity kept narrow to Customer-provided content and our breach of law.

ops.text: Vendor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer and its Affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Services, Deliverables, or Vendor Technology infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) Vendor's breach of Applicable Law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor; or (d) Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud.

Customer shall indemnify Vendor against third-party claims to the extent arising out of content or materials Customer provides to Vendor for use in the Services or Customer's breach of Applicable Law. Customer has no other indemnification obligation under this Agreement.

The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party prompt written notice of a claim, with delay excusing the indemnifying Party only to the extent it is prejudiced. The indemnifying Party shall control the defence with counsel reasonably acceptable to the indemnified Party, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying Party's expense and may participate with its own counsel at its own cost. A settlement that imposes a non-monetary obligation, admission of liability, or unreimbursed payment on the indemnified Party requires its prior written consent.

Vendor's indemnity under Section 20.1(a) does not apply to the extent a claim arises from Customer's modification of a Deliverable other than as documented, Customer's combination of the Services with items not supplied or recommended by Vendor where the claim arises solely from that combination, or Vendor's compliance with Customer's written specifications.

If an infringement claim is made or the Services or a Deliverable is held to infringe, Vendor shall at its expense procure the rights necessary for Customer's continued use, or modify or replace the affected item with a functionally equivalent non-infringing item. If neither option is reasonably available, Customer may terminate the affected Services or Deliverable and Vendor shall refund prepaid Fees for the terminated portion together with Fees paid for any Deliverable Customer can no longer reasonably use.

proposal.summary: Insert a new Section 20 (Indemnification) with a Vendor IP/misconduct indemnity, standard defence procedure, narrow Customer indemnity, and the infringement remedies cross-referenced by Section 9.3.

quote: infringes a third party's intellectual property and cannot provide the remedies required by Section 20.5.
rationale: The Agreement has no indemnification section: the outline jumps from Section 19 (Warranties) to Section 21 (Limitation of Liability), and no "indemnify", "defend" or "hold harmless" obligation appears anywhere. Yet Section 9.3 relies on "the remedies required by Section 20.5", and Sections 19.4, 19.5, 21.3 and 30.5 all presuppose indemnity obligations, leaving dangling cross-references. Vendor therefore owes us no IP infringement or misconduct indemnity, which is the playbook walk-away scenario. We inserted a new Section 20 giving the preferred Vendor defence/indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, Vendor-caused Customer Data incidents and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, standard claim procedure, usual IP exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies (curing the Section 9.3 reference), while keeping Customer's indemnity narrow to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law. No super-cap is needed because Section 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.

quote: 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.
rationale: Section 21 meets our preferred position in full. 21.1 sets a single mutual cap at the greater of (a) Fees paid or payable by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim event and (b) USD 1,000,000, expressly stated to be mutual — neither party is uncapped and the basis is "paid or payable" rather than the narrower "paid". The "Fees" definition (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees (not an illusory set-up fee), and §2.1 commits USD 2,000,000 of annual spend, so the fee-based limb is meaningful. 21.2 excludes indirect/consequential damages mutually and helpfully confirms data restoration, replacement services, breach notification and incident response costs are direct damages. 21.3 places confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other party's IP outside the cap, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not "damages". No competing cap or one-sided liability language appears elsewhere (§18.2 confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities). Separate note for the indemnity rule: Section 20 (indemnification, cross-referenced in §9.3 and §21.3) is absent from the document, so the indemnity carve-out currently has nothing to attach to; that gap is outside the scope of this cap rule and no redline to Section 21 is warranted.

quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full. 24.1 permits Customer assignment without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets, subject only to prompt notice and assignee assumption. 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld for a capable, financially sound assignee), plus an absolute bar on assigning to a direct Customer competitor. 24.3 does not swallow 24.1 because it is expressly limited to "other assignments," operating only as a residual catch-all outside the 24.1/24.2 carve-outs, with a mutual, reasonableness-qualified consent standard. 24.4 removes any Vendor right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on Customer's change of control, closing the walk-away risk, and requires Vendor cooperation with administrative changes for a permitted successor. 13.3 tracks Section 24 by allowing licence rights to transfer to an Affiliate or successor on a permitted assignment, so a successor is not stranded. No "deemed an assignment" trap or change-of-control trigger appears elsewhere; the only other assignment reference (9.2) concerns insolvency-related general assignments for creditors. No redline needed.

quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
rationale: Section 7.2 (p0026) conditions our right to engage another provider on first disclosing any more favourable third-party offer and matching it for Vendor. That is a disclose-and-match gate that functions as de facto exclusivity plus a most-favoured-customer commitment binding Customer: we cannot freely source elsewhere without giving Vendor a right of first refusal on price, and it is unlimited as to category, duration, and has no performance-based exit. It also directly contradicts Section 12.3 (p0044), in which Vendor acknowledges Customer has made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment, and Section 2.2's precedence ladder does not resolve an internal conflict within the Agreement. No other exclusivity provision binds Customer (the remaining "exclusive" references concern the non-exclusive licence, remedies, and jurisdiction). Preferred position is no exclusivity obligation on Customer, so we delete the clause; the fallback (narrow category, 12 months, automatic termination on missed service levels) is offered in the comment.
